findings.reason: the population a node must count and the count it reports against are fixed by this clause, so the 56/48 mislabel sends the measure at the wrong set unless the sentence states the class (56) or the waiting set (48).
findings.text: §6's first bullet requires the equivalent-electron population to carry `equivalent_electron` "or is listed by name with the source evidence for leaving it, the fifty-six names of the first rewrite's waiting list among them", but the class has 56 members of which only 48 wait: §11 at plan.html:157 states "Eight names are renamed and live; forty-eight wait", and `live-rewrite-manifest.json` records `totals_by_class["equivalent-electron"] = 56` with no status on any of the 56 entries. The clause therefore names a 56-name "waiting list" that does not exist, and a node measuring a 56-name waiting list finds 48 and must decide whether to treat the 8 already renamed/live names as waiting, unmeasured, or in-scope

response_events.note: The clause now names the class of fifty-six recorded by the first rewrite and states that eight are since renamed and forty-eight are not.
